transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Yes, please start by cleaning the lint filter (usually at the bottom front) and checking if you dried a full wash load. Washer-dryers can only dry about half the amount they wash; drying an overloaded drum will leave clothes damp and cause fluff to scorch on the heater, creating that smell.

I usually dry a full wash load, about 8-9kg, straight after washing. The smell is like burning dust or scorched fabric, and the top of the machine gets very hot. I've kept using it though. Where's the filter on this one?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. On most Hotpoint washer-dryers, the lint filter is located behind a small access flap at the bottom right of the front panel. To find it: unplug the machine first for safety, open that flap, and pull out the filter (it may be a mesh cylinder or a flat panel). You should also see a condenser unit just above or next to it (a plastic grille you can slide out). Please check if there is a thick layer of fluff in the filter or on the condenser fins. Please do not use the machine again until it has been checked. A qualified engineer needs to inspect the internal components to ensure there is no fire risk or electrical fault before it can be used safely.

candidates: Lint filter or condenser blocked (airflow restriction) (high)
Drying heater element or thermal cut-out fault (low)

claimsRejected.claim: Because you have noticed a burning smell and the top of the machine getting very hot, this strongly suggests that fluff has built up and is scorching on the heating element due to restricted airflow (exacerbated by drying an 8-9kg load).

candidates: Restricted airflow due to overloaded drum and blocked filter/condenser causing fluff scorching on the heater (high)
Faulty drying thermostat or heater element insulation failure (medium)
